title: Computer Basics & Office Skills Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of hardware, operating systems, MS Office, the internet, and data science fundamentals.

questions.question: What does CPU stand for?
questions.explain: CPU stands for Central Processing Unit, the chip that executes instructions and does the computer's core calculations.

questions.question: Which type of storage retains data without power (non-volatile)?
questions.explain: ROM, SSDs, and HDDs are non-volatile, meaning they keep stored data even after power is turned off, unlike RAM or cache.

questions.question: In Microsoft Excel, which function calculates the average of a range?
questions.explain: AVERAGE() adds up the values in a range and divides by how many there are, giving the arithmetic mean.

questions.question: What does HTTP stand for?
options: B. Hyperlink and Text Transition Protocol
C. Host Transfer and Tunneling Protocol
questions.explain: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the standard protocol browsers use to request and receive web pages.

questions.question: What is the primary job of an Operating System?
options: A. Manage hardware resources and provide services to applications
questions.explain: An OS manages CPU, memory, storage, and devices, and provides a platform of services on which applications run.

questions.question: In Excel, which shortcut autofills a selected cell formula down a column?
questions.explain: Ctrl+D fills the contents or formula of the top cell in a selection down into the cells below it.

questions.question: What is RAM used for?
options: A. Permanent storage of the OS
C. Temporary fast storage for actively running programs
questions.explain: RAM holds data and instructions that running programs need right now, offering fast access but losing contents when power is off.

questions.question: Which protocol secures web traffic by encrypting it?
questions.explain: HTTPS wraps HTTP traffic in TLS encryption, protecting data from being read or tampered with in transit.

questions.question: In Python's pandas, what does df.head() return?
options: D. The data types of each column
questions.explain: By default, df.head() previews a DataFrame by returning its first 5 rows.

questions.question: What is the function of a router on a network?
options: A. Connect devices within the same LAN by MAC address
B. Forward packets between networks based on IP address
questions.explain: A router examines IP addresses to forward data packets between different networks, such as a home LAN and the internet.

questions.question: In Word, which shortcut adds a page break?
questions.explain: Ctrl+Enter inserts a manual page break, pushing the following text onto a new page.

questions.question: What does SSD stand for?
questions.explain: SSD stands for Solid State Drive, which stores data on flash memory chips with no moving parts, making it fast and durable.

questions.question: What Python library is primarily used for numerical array computations?
questions.explain: NumPy provides fast, efficient multi-dimensional arrays and the core numerical operations many other data science libraries build on.

questions.question: In PowerPoint, what is a 'Slide Master'?
options: A. The first slide in a presentation
B. A template that controls the design of all slides
C. The slide with the most content
D. A locked slide that cannot be edited
questions.explain: The Slide Master defines the layout, fonts, and colors inherited by every slide, letting you update the whole presentation's design at once.

questions.question: What is an IP address?
options: B. A type of network cable
C. A numerical label assigned to each device on a network
questions.explain: An IP address is a numerical label that identifies and locates a device on a network so data can be routed to it.

questions.question: What does DNS resolve?
options: A. MAC addresses to IP addresses
B. IP addresses to physical locations
D. Domain names to IP addresses
questions.explain: DNS (Domain Name System) translates human-readable domain names into the IP addresses computers use to find each other.

questions.question: Which Excel function looks up a value in a table by row?
questions.explain: VLOOKUP searches the first column of a table vertically and returns a value from a specified column in that matching row.

questions.question: What is 'virtualization' in computing?
options: B. Running multiple virtual machines on one physical host
C. Backing up data to the cloud
questions.explain: Virtualization uses software to create multiple isolated virtual machines that share the resources of one physical computer.

questions.question: In data science, what is a 'DataFrame' in pandas?
options: C. A 2D tabular data structure with labeled axes
D. A Python function for data cleaning
questions.explain: A DataFrame is pandas' core structure: a two-dimensional table with labeled rows and columns, similar to a spreadsheet.

questions.question: What does the 'motherboard' do in a computer?
options: D. Connects and allows communication between all hardware components
questions.explain: The motherboard is the main circuit board that physically connects the CPU, RAM, storage, and other components so they can communicate.

questions.question: In Word, 'Track Changes' is used to:
options: A. Record edits made so reviewers can see and accept/reject them
C. Sync documents to the cloud automatically
questions.explain: Track Changes marks every insertion, deletion, and edit so reviewers can see who changed what and accept or reject it.

questions.question: What is a 'cookie' in web browsing?
options: B. A small data file stored by a browser to remember session info
D. A type of web server
questions.explain: A cookie is a small piece of data a website asks the browser to store, used to remember logins, preferences, and session state.

questions.question: Which pandas method removes rows with missing values?
questions.explain: df.dropna() removes rows (or columns) that contain missing (NaN) values, while fillna() would fill them in instead.

questions.question: What does 'cloud computing' mean?
options: B. Processing data inside a physical cloud server room only
D. Delivering computing services (servers, storage, software) over the internet
questions.explain: Cloud computing delivers servers, storage, databases, and software as on-demand services over the internet instead of local hardware.

questions.question: In Excel, what does the '$' symbol do in a cell reference like '$A$1'?
options: A. Makes the reference absolute so it does not change when the formula is copied
B. Formats the cell as currency
C. Refers to a named range
D. Calculates the sum of column A
questions.explain: The $ locks the column and/or row of a reference, so it stays fixed on $A$1 instead of shifting when the formula is copied elsewhere.
